name: National Gallery of Victoria
notes: National Gallery of Victoria, St Kilda Road (Roy Grounds, 1968): a long, nearly windowless two-storey block of grey bluestone, about 150 m by 74 m, set in a moat; the tall round-headed entrance arch on St Kilda Road with the Water Wall behind it; three internal courtyards; the Great Hall at the back under Leonard French's stained-glass ceiling; the sculpture garden behind. Footprint, the moat's line and the road from the ground file (the real building is turned a few degrees off north; the model is square to it). Written from general knowledge. Guessed: courtyard sizes and positions, the height (about 18 m), the roof lanterns. Bluestone drawn in the grey 'concrete' material. No photographs were available.
